column3: MT 84:1–2; the following verses of this psalm are MT +1. Close to the Hebrew; “On the Gittith” is rendered “On an instrument of Gath,” and the plural “dwelling places” “Your tabernacle.”
Close to the Hebrew; יְרַנְּנוּ (“sing for joy”) is rendered “cry out.”
Close to the Hebrew; צִפּוֹר (“a bird”) is rendered “the sparrow.”
Close to the Hebrew; “highways are in their heart” is rendered “Whose heart is set on pilgrimage.”
NKJV reads בְּרָכוֹת (“blessings”) as “pools,” a different vowel reading, and “early rain” as “The rain.”
Close to the Hebrew; “he appears” is rendered “Each one appears.”
Close to the Hebrew; “to stand at the threshold” is rendered “to be a doorkeeper.”
Close to the Hebrew; “favor and honor” is rendered “grace and glory,” and “in blamelessness” “uprightly.”
